established: drm_dev_unregister removes user-visible clients/minors and invokes unload only if provided. The reviewed Rust VTABLE provides no M4 pump-join hook.
File postclose is invoked by drm_file_free, while VFS file ownership remains held through release; that protects file callback code but completion fences do not prove pump callback return.
Gravity Device::new already allocates with release=None, performs fallible pinned data init, releases via temporary vtable on init error, and publishes full VTABLE only on success.
Aurora uses the corresponding temporary no-release constructor pattern and actual drop_in_place in initialized device release.
Gravity release still suppresses the destructor, so runtime RTKit destruction is not established by final device reference release.

Actual RtKit::drop calls apple_rtkit_free before freeing callback data; C free stops mailbox and destroys its workqueue before freeing buffers. This is a callback-join boundary only if the owning destructor actually executes.
Aurora cleanup queue ownership is outside platform registration; destructor runs after producer boundaries. Its assumptions cannot be copied without equivalent M4 joins.
open: Trace last DeviceRef release contexts, especially canceled jobs and running pump callbacks, before enabling synchronous scheduler/RTKit destruction.
Establish unbind ordering before devres invalidates mapped I/O, prevent new producers, and join pump callbacks; do not use global system queue flush.
Retain firmware-visible pages on failed shutdown without retaining callable module callbacks after unload.
